title: Calibration harness and canary + auto-fallback flow for FP8/INT8 quantized profiles
creator: Aisha Kumar
body:
Summary:
We need an end-to-end calibration and validation harness plus an automated canary rollout that will enable FP8 and INT8 quantized model variants to be promoted to production only when they meet defined accuracy and latency guardrails. If a quantized variant fails quality checks during canary traffic, the system must automatically fallback to the unquantized baseline (or a higher-precision variant) with zero-downtime and record evidence for post-mortem and model improvement.

Motivation & context:
- Quantization reduces cost and inference latency but can introduce accuracy regressions that are workload-dependent.
- We currently have manual, ad-hoc calibration runs for some models and no standardized auto-fallback policy. This leads to customer-facing regressions when teams prematurely switch traffic to quantized variants.
- Goal: provide a developer-facing workflow so model owners can: (1) generate calibration profiles, (2) run accuracy checks against canonical prompt sets, (3) canary a quantized variant under real traffic, and (4) auto-fallback if quality thresholds are violated.

Scope & deliverables:
1) Calibration harness: a reproducible job that runs per-model calibration using provided calibration corpora and exports a reproducible quant profile (FP8/INT8), calibration artifacts, and a deterministic seed for any stochastic ops. Output stored in model-artifacts bucket with metadata (model version, dataset sha, quant flags).
2) Accuracy validator: evaluation pipeline that runs the candidate quantized variant against:
   - golden prompt set (per-model) with labeled references
   - production-sampled holdout traffic (anonymized) for real-world distribution checks
   Metrics collected: exact-match (EM), BLEU/ROUGE (where applicable), token-level KL, and task-specific metrics (e.g., F1 for NER).
   The validator will compute delta vs baseline and produce a pass/fail decision based on configurable thresholds (example: EM drop <= 0.5% absolute OR task-specific drop <= 1% relative).
3) Canary rollout orchestration: a rollout controller that can route a configurable fraction of traffic to quantized variants and monitor live metrics (latency P50/P95, error rate, model output quality by sampled evaluations).
4) Auto-fallback policy: automated action that switches traffic back to a safe variant when thresholds are crossed. Requirements:
   - fallback must be atomic and preserve in-flight requests where possible (graceful draining),
   - fallback reason and metric evidence must be logged and attached to the model artifact,
   - notify stakeholders (Slack + email webhook) and create a Linear incident ticket (auto-link).
5) Observability & audit: dashboards showing calibration job history, validator results, canary rollouts, and fallback incidents. Retain artifacts for 90 days.

Acceptance criteria:
- Calibration harness can produce a quantization profile for an example model (Llama-2-style) and artifact saved with metadata.
- Validator passes for at least one FP8 and one INT8 candidate on the golden prompt set with metrics recorded.
- Canary rollout can be started with traffic weight controls and automatically scales back to baseline upon threshold violation within 5 minutes of breach.
- Automated notifications and rollback ticket creation present and verified in staging.

Implementation notes & trade-offs:
- Calibration dataset size: larger corpora -> better calibration but longer wall-clock. We'll provide a default small 'fast' corpus and a recommended 'production' corpus.
- FP8 is promising on throughput but can be more brittle; the validator should use conservative thresholds for FP8 until we gather more telemetry.
- For latency-sensitive endpoints we should prefer a staged promotion: canary (1%), ramp (10%), then full. Consider allowing teams to opt-out of full rollout.
- Storing raw sample outputs for privacy-sensitive workloads is disallowed; use hashed prompts/metadata and store only evaluation scores unless customer permits.

Work breakdown (high-level):
- ENG task A: calibration harness + artifact schema (Luis)
- ENG task B: validator pipeline and threshold config (Aisha)
- ENG task C: rollout controller integration with router and runtime (On-call infra/Marco)
- ENG task D: fallback action hook, notifications, and Linear ticket auto-creation (SRE)
- ENG task E: dashboards & retention policy (Observability)

Open questions / decisions required:
- Threshold defaults: product to confirm conservative defaults for FP8/INT8 (suggested: 0.5% abs drop for high-priority QA metrics).
- Who owns golden prompt sets per model? Recommend model owner in Research/Applied ML.
- Can we anonymize sampled production traffic enough to use as validator input? Legal needs to sign off.

Risks & mitigations:
- False positives in validator due to small eval corpora -> mitigate by requiring both golden set and sampled traffic checks to pass.
- State explosion from many quant profiles -> add retention/garbage-collection and encourage canonical profiles per major model family.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: calibration harness MVP + artifact storage (staging)
- Week 2: validator integration + local experiments (generate FP8/INT8 profiles for 2 models)
- Week 3: canary controller + auto-fallback hook (staged rollout on internal traffic)
- Week 4: observability + docs + signoff -> release to runtime-1.22

- GitHub PR template: github.com/redwood-inference/quant/pulls (placeholder)

comments: 2025-02-21 - Luis Ortega: Spiked on calibration in staging. FP8 path required small dtype handling in the runtime; need a kernel flag. Opened ENG-9180 for kernel flagging.

2025-02-25 - Aisha Kumar: Validator now supports golden prompts and computes EM/ROUGE deltas. Early FP8 run on model-x shows 0.8% EM regression on the small corpus; we should tighten thresholds or expand corpus.
2025-02-27 - Marco Li: Router integration prototype routes 2% traffic to canary and exposes metric streams. Need to add graceful draining to avoid dropped requests during fallback.

2025-03-03 - Product (Rosa Bennett): Confirmed conservative defaults: 0.5% absolute EM drop for NLU intents, 1% relative drop for generation BLEU/ROUGE. Legal to evaluate anonymized sampled traffic next week.
